_comment: Shared cross-language fixture cases for the .agentic/ root resolver. Consumed by BOTH hooks/tests/test-repo-root.js and hooks/tests/test-repo-root.py, so a JS/Python resolver divergence surfaces as one suite going red against a fixture neither owns. Each case describes a directory layout to build under a temp root and the expected resolveAgenticCwdWithDiagnostics() outcome relative to that temp root.

cases.description: startDir IS the repo root (has .git as a dir).
startDir is one level below the repo root.
startDir is four levels below the repo root.
Repo root's .git is a FILE (linked git worktree shape). Existence-only check must still find it.
Repo root's .git is a DIR (ordinary clone shape), tested explicitly alongside the file form.
startDir drifted two levels below a worktree root whose .git is a FILE.
No .git anywhere up to the temp root boundary - falls back to the realpath'd startDir unchanged, foundGitAncestor false.
startDir is a symlink to a drifted directory inside the repo. Both resolvers must realpath first and agree post-realpath.

.git exists at an intermediate level but is chmod 000 (EACCES on stat/access from a non-root process) - existence check must still find it (or, on platforms where EACCES prevents even existence detection, must not throw and must continue walking).

expect.note: existsSync/os.path.exists on the parent dir entry does not require read permission on .git itself on POSIX; this case is a defensive regression guard against a future implementation that stats INTO .git rather than checking its existence at the parent listing level

cases.description: Exactly MAX_DEPTH (64) levels of drift below the repo root - must still resolve.
MAX_DEPTH+1 (65) levels of drift below the repo root - beyond the walk bound, must fall back (foundGitAncestor false) rather than finding the root or throwing.

expect.note: no .git at any level in this layout, so this case tests the walk terminating cleanly at MAX_DEPTH rather than an off-by-one on a git ancestor that exists just past the bound
